- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.4) or volatile, model underestimates; add 3–7% to forecast mean to compensate for downward bias.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 2–5% downward adjustment to first 5–7 forecast days.
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore it; reduce forecast slope downward by 10–20%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2), model often drifts upward; apply 2–5% downward correction to avoid overconfidence bias.
